results.rubric_item: Explain a key network effect involving Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) who develop services on the largest cloud platforms to maximize their audience, which in turn attracts more users to these platforms.
results.reason: The article describes the ISV network effect: ISVs develop for the bigger providers, and providers with the most customers attract the most ISVs, forming reinforcing ecosystems.
results.evidence: ISVs find it costly to support more than one platform and so "typically develop services for one or a few cloud providers, notably the bigger ones," while "cloud providers with the most customers attract the most ISVs, creating ecosystems around a few cloud providers."

results.rubric_item: Explain another network effect related to developer familiarity, where developers prefer platforms they have already been trained on, and targeted offers to universities reinforce this.
results.reason: The article explains developer familiarity as a distinct network effect (availability of developers/engineers familiar with a provider), though it does not mention university-targeted offers.
results.evidence: Developer familiarity operates as its own network effect: the Dutch ACM notes that "using the services of large cloud providers offers the best chance of finding developers,"... while Japan's JFTC found in its own customer survey that 23.1% of IaaS customers and 20.5% of PaaS customers cited the availability of "a large number of introduction support providers and engineers...who can deal with that cloud service" as a reason for choosing their current provider.

results.rubric_item: Point out that economies of scope stem from hyperscale providers offering seamless, integrated service suites, thereby driving user adoption of their cloud offerings.

results.evidence: hyperscalers' "conglomerate structure" lets them "develop discount systems, tariff and non-tariff benefits or cross-subsidies" that favor their own cloud offering... "large hyperscalers organised into ecosystems enjoy competitive advantages over suppliers offering more limited catalogues of services."
